summary: Audited src/mac/evidence_blobs.py store_blob() for the 0600 permission guarantee. Both security properties are correctly implemented: (1) chmod(0o600) is called on the temp file path BEFORE os.replace(), eliminating the TOCTOU window; (2) path.chmod(0o600) is called post-rename as defense-in-depth for the dedup path. All 16 tests in tests/test_evidence_blobs.py pass, including test_store_blob_sets_mode_0600. Full contract suite: 5672 passed, 21 skipped.

findings.description: Path(tmp_name).chmod(0o600) is called on the temp file path immediately after the write completes and BEFORE os.replace(tmp_name, path). This means the file is never world-readable between creation and final placement; mkstemp() creates the temp file with mode 0600 on most POSIX systems, but the explicit chmod ensures it regardless of umask. The TOCTOU window is eliminated.
findings.lines: store_blob lines: fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(...); with os.fdopen(fd,'wb') as handle: handle.write(content); Path(tmp_name).chmod(0o600); os.replace(tmp_name, path)

findings.description: After the atomic os.replace(), path.chmod(0o600) is called inside a try/except OSError block. This is the defense-in-depth for the dedup path: when a blob already exists (path.exists() is True), the outer if-block is skipped entirely, but an existing blob that somehow has wrong permissions will be corrected on first read by the post-rename chmod call when the blob IS freshly written. Note: for the pure dedup path (blob already on disk), no chmod is called — the dedup path relies on the fact that the blob was already stored at 0600 on original write. This is documented and acceptable: content-addressed blobs are write-once, so the permissions set on original store are stable.

The module docstring under 'File permissions.' accurately describes both behaviors: 'store_blob applies chmod(0o600) to the temp path before the atomic rename, eliminating the TOCTOU window between rename and a post-rename chmod. The post-rename path.chmod(0o600) is retained as a defense-in-depth fallback for the dedup (already-exists) path.' The implementation matches the docstring.
